A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Proteus research despite the revised title and conference formatting. All pages, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification, segmentation, depth-estimation, robustness, and distillation-ablation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The token, feature, and masked-patch objectives, projection heads, equal loss weights, and teacher/student arrangements are unchanged. Both versions use only the token objective when distilling CLIP. Specifying last-layer features in v2 clarifies implementation rather than establishing a different method.

E1.justification: The proxy datasets, classification benchmarks, dense-prediction tasks, robustness datasets, and out-of-domain evaluations are retained. The headline changes from 15 to 19 benchmarks by incorporating four robustness benchmarks already reported in v1; Table 22 lists the same datasets.

E2.justification: Figure 2 replaces the DeiT-B/16 comparison point with iBOT-L/16 and MAE-H/14 points in the training-data versus fine-grained-accuracy comparison. Comparator membership in the matched main-text and appendix tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: Figure 2 introduces the iBOT-L/16 and MAE-H/14 comparison configurations, including a newly represented Huge model size. Existing Proteus training budgets, batch sizes, probing procedures, preprocessing, and dense-prediction settings remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The dataset-bias and objective ablations move from v1 Tables 8–9 to v2 Tables 1–2 without changes. Proxy-data, weight-inheritance, robustness, teacher-choice, efficiency, and projection-head analyses are also retained. The redesigned overview redisplays existing analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both retain the same speculative attribution of a small accuracy difference to linear-probing variance.

E6.justification: Figure 2 adds fine-grained average-accuracy results for iBOT-L/16 and MAE-H/14, both below Proteus-L/14. All matched tabulated scores are identical. The revised radar chart summarizes previously reported results rather than demonstrating new Proteus performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 and their mathematical definitions are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theoretical propositions, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract expands the stated parity claim from 15 to 19 benchmarks. The introduction and Figure 1 extend the emphasis from Large-model parity and a Small-model shortfall to matching DINOv2 across scales, while elevating the already evaluated Proteus-Tiny into an explicit contribution.

C2.justification: The substantive explanations concerning dataset bias, proxy-data diversity, teacher-size gaps, and robustness remain unchanged. Both versions retain the limitations concerning unverified larger-data training and matching the teacher's patch size; broader-impact edits largely restate existing scalability and multimodal aspirations.

D1.justification: Section 2.1 specifies last-layer features instead of intermediate features. Conversely, v2 omits v1 Section 4.1's explicit statement that the ablation excludes DeiT's extra distillation token. Appendix implementation details, hardware, timing information, and code-access links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related Work adds few-sample and data-free distillation references, including Li et al. (2020), Chen et al. (2019), DeepInversion, and DearKD, while removing several generic distillation references and Asano et al. (2019). It clarifies the distinction between prior task-specific compression and Proteus's task-agnostic compression with limited data.

P1.justification: The core experimental narrative is substantially reorganized: design ablations and the DeiT comparison now precede DINOv2 benchmark results, and the separate Analysis section is absorbed into Empirical Validation. The title, introductory contribution summary, section terminology, and citation style are also revised.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redesigned from individual benchmark axes at one model scale to grouped metrics and multiple scales. Figure 2 changes comparison points, legend, and vertical range. Core tables are relocated with the reordered narrative, and the document adopts the ICLR layout throughout.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies the limited-data, task-agnostic setting, adds relevant research context, and makes the design evidence easier to follow by placing ablations before benchmark comparisons. These provide a modest overall gain. Numerical evidence is essentially unchanged, and the broader parity wording remains qualified by performance gaps retained in the tables.
